messages.content:
You are FOXO's lifestyle coach. Using the doctor's review of a member's lab results, write a practical diet and lifestyle plan for a member living in India.

Rules:
1. Respect the member's diet, allergies and conditions in every item:
   - vegetarian: no meat, fish, seafood or eggs
   - eggetarian: eggs are fine; no meat, fish or seafood
   - vegan: no animal products, including dairy, ghee and honey
   - jain: vegetarian with no eggs, no honey, no onion or garlic, and no root vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar)
   - allergies: never include the allergen in any form
   - diabetes: no sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets or sweetened drinks
2. Each diet recommendation must target one of the abnormal biomarkers in the doctor's findings. Put that biomarker's name in linked_biomarker, written as in the findings.
3. Never contradict the doctor's lifestyle_restrictions. If the doctor restricts exercise, suggest only gentle activity such as an easy walk, and tell the member to follow the doctor's advice.
4. Do not recommend medicines or supplements and never give doses. If a supplement might help, say "ask your FOXO doctor".
5. Use everyday Indian foods (dal, millets, seasonal sabzi, sprouts and so on) and be specific about portions and timing.
6. Put foods to eat in diet_recommendations and foods to limit or avoid in foods_to_avoid.
7. retest_in_weeks is usually 12.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"DietRecommendation": {"properties": {"item": {"title": "Item", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "linked_biomarker": {"title": "Linked Biomarker", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["item", "rationale", "linked_biomarker"], "title": "DietRecommendation", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"focus_areas": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Focus Areas", "type": "array"}, "diet_recommendations": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DietRecommendation"}, "title": "Diet Recommendations", "type": "array"}, "foods_to_avoid": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Foods To Avoid", "type": "array"}, "activity": {"title": "Activity", "type": "string"}, "sleep": {"title": "Sleep", "type": "string"}, "retest_in_weeks": {"title": "Retest In Weeks", "type": "integer"}}, "required": ["focus_areas", "diet_recommendations", "activity", "sleep", "retest_in_weeks"], "title": "CoachPlan", "type": "object"}

response: {"focus_areas":["Lower triglycerides through reduced refined carbohydrates and added sugars","Lower LDL cholesterol with soluble fibre and healthier fats","Address vitamin D insufficiency with clinician-guided testing and supplementation if advised","Keep all meals Jain-compatible and strictly peanut-free","Complete cardiology review and repeat fasting lipid panel as advised"],"diet_recommendations":[{"item":"At breakfast, have 1 katori cooked plain oats or barley porridge 3–4 days a week; do not add sugar, jaggery or honey.","rationale":"Soluble fibre from oats and barley helps lower LDL cholesterol when eaten regularly.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"},{"item":"At lunch and dinner, fill half the plate with seasonal non-root sabzi such as lauki, tinda, bhindi, beans or parval; take 1 katori dal or mung sprouts and 2 phulka or 1 cup cooked millet instead of large portions of white rice or maida.","rationale":"Replacing refined grains with whole millets, dal and non-starchy vegetables helps lower triglycerides.","linked_biomarker":"triglycerides"},{"item":"Replace sweetened drinks, sweets and fruit juices with water, unsweetened buttermilk or 1 small whole fruit such as guava or apple at snack time.","rationale":"Reducing added sugars and sweetened drinks is important for lowering triglycerides.","linked_biomarker":"triglycerides"},{"item":"Include 1 cup vitamin-D-fortified milk or curd with breakfast or lunch daily if available; get 15–20 minutes of morning sunlight on arms and face 3–4 days a week as tolerated, and ask your FOXO doctor whether vitamin D supplementation is needed.","rationale":"Supports vitamin D status; supplementation decisions should be clinician-guided.","linked_biomarker":"vitamin_d"},{"item":"Use about 1 teaspoon of cooking oil per meal such as mustard, rice bran or olive oil; prefer steaming, boiling or sautéing, and keep deep-fried foods and extra ghee/butter to occasional small amounts.","rationale":"Limiting saturated fat and fried foods helps lower LDL cholesterol.","linked_biomarker":"ldl"},{"item":"Finish dinner by 7:30–8:00 pm and keep a 12-hour overnight fast; avoid late-night snacks, and if hungry after dinner take 1 cup unsweetened buttermilk.","rationale":"An earlier dinner and overnight fast can help improve triglyceride levels.","linked_biomarker":"triglycerides"}],"foods_to_avoid":["Peanut, peanut butter, peanut chikki, peanut oil, and any packaged food labelled 'may contain peanut' or processed in a facility with peanut","Sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets, mithai, sweetened drinks, fruit juices and sherbet","Refined flour (maida), white bread, bakery items and large portions of polished white rice","Deep-fried snacks such as samosa, pakora and puri, and excessive ghee or butter","Onion, garlic, potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and other root vegetables to keep the plan Jain-compatible","Eggs, meat, fish and seafood to keep the plan Jain-compatible"],"activity":"No exercise restriction is noted. Aim for 30 minutes of brisk walking 5 days a week, starting with 10–15 minutes after meals if needed; add gentle yoga or stretching 2 days a week. Follow your doctor's advice and attend the cardiology review before significantly intensifying activity.","sleep":"Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep nightly with fixed sleep and wake times. Avoid screens for 30 minutes before bed and keep dinner early.","retest_in_weeks":12}
